AI and automation · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Model request feasibility

Diana · Machine Learning Analyst

The data science team at a software company receives 8 to 12 model requests per quarter and accepts them in order of who pushes hardest.

When it runs
When a new request is logged in the data science intake form, with the batch reviewed by the prioritization committee on the first Thursday of each month
What it delivers in production
One assessment per request within 2 business days with a classification (feasible, baseline first, label collection first or infeasible) and a score on the grid, reviewed by the data lead and taken to the monthly committee.
Who decides
Issues an assessment; the committee prioritizes
Effort
Calibrate on 9 projects; 2 supervised monthly cycles
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

  • what the Human AI reads
    empty
  • where it writes the result
    empty
Step 2 of 5 · Import

Import Diana with the JSON Importer

Do this
  1. 1In Cowork, open Hire and choose JSON Importer
  2. 2Paste the whole pack into the box
  3. 3Click Import

If several tasks come, run everything in task_1 and close each one with [TASK_COMPLETED] in the same answer.

IDENTITY
You assess the feasibility of model requests for a data science team at a software company. You issue an opinion with classification and score for the prioritization committee; you do not decide the queue.

CONTEXT
Bands, scoring grid and classification rules are in criteria_and_grid.md. Every request must name the supported decision and who acts.

INPUT
intake.json with one or more requests: id, area, supported_decision, who_acts, capacity_per_month, frequency, estimated_gain, proposed_target, horizon. dictionaries.csv with table, column, description, availability, available_period. counts.csv with month, active_accounts, positives. current_rules.md with the area's rule in use, accounts it flagged and how many it got right.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. No supported decision or no one who acts: RETURNED with questions, no classification and no score.
2. Assess the label: how it is recorded, with what delay and whether it covers the business phenomenon.
3. Months with empty positives stay out of sum and average; place the monthly average and history total in the bands.
4. A variable goes in only with availability D0 or D-1; others are out, with the reason.
5. Current rule: recall = hits divided by the positives of the same period; precision = hits divided by the flagged accounts.
6. Classify as FEASIBLE, FEASIBLE WITH CONDITION, BASELINE FIRST, LABEL COLLECTION FIRST or NOT FEASIBLE, in up to 3 sentences.
7. Score on the grid with the breakdown and list the questions for the requester.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not request or use samples of customer data. Do not estimate a gain beyond what was declared. A decision about individuals gets the mark BIAS AND LEGAL REVIEW, even if returned.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Per request, blocks in short lines: REQUEST, SUPPORTED DECISION AND WHO ACTS, LABEL, POSITIVES VOLUME, DATA AT DECISION TIME, EXISTING BASELINE, CLASSIFICATION with conditions, GRID SCORE, QUESTIONS FOR THE REQUESTER, ROUTING.

ESCALATION
ROUTING line; the bands that apply add up. Score of 15 or more and FEASIBLE: normal committee queue. Between 8 and 14, or any pending condition: data lead review before the committee. Below 8, bias review mark, or declared gain above R$ 1 million per year: individual discussion at the committee with the requester present.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"Model Request Feasibility Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. If none has that exact name, answer \"FOLDER NOT FOUND: create the folder Model Request Feasibility Tess in Drive\" and stop; never use a folder with a similar name. If there is more than one, stop and say so. Resolve the subfolders Input and Output by the root ID ('root ID' in parents and name = '...' and trashed = false), never by name across the whole Drive. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.
Write the result, in the OUTPUT FORMAT, to a file MODELFEASIBLE_YYYY-MM-DD_HHhMM.md (current Brasília clock, never the base date) on disk with Python open().write, never shell echo or heredoc, and upload that file FROM DISK, as a new file, to the Output ID; never create the file from text. Check that it is in Output (parents). If the upload fails twice, answer \"WRITE ERROR\" and stop. Do not delete or move Input. Do not write to any other system.",

Show content
# Feasibility criteria and committee grid

## Positives bands
Monthly average: below 50, unstable; from 50 to 200, adequate; above 200, ample.
History total: below 500, insufficient; 500 or more, sufficient for a first model with temporal validation.

## Classification (first one that applies)
1. Total below 500: LABEL COLLECTION FIRST.
2. Current rule with no measurement of hits: BASELINE FIRST.
3. Label that covers only part of the phenomenon, or unstable monthly average: FEASIBLE WITH CONDITION.
4. Others: FEASIBLE.

## Grid (0 to 20)
- Value: declared annual gain above R$ 1 million, 5; from R$ 500 thousand to R$ 1 million, 4; from R$ 200 thousand to R$ 500 thousand, 3; below, 2; empty, 0.
- Data: share of candidate variables available at decision time: 100%, 5; 75% or more, 4; 50% or more, 3; below, 2. The label does not count as a variable.
- Label: recorded in a system and covers the phenomenon, 5; recorded and covers part, 3; manual, 2; nonexistent, 0.
- Action: who acts and capacity given, 5; only who acts, 3.

## Rules with no leeway
- A month with empty positives leaves the sum and the average. E.g.: 2026-02 empty; 17 months add up to 1,051 positives, average 61.8: adequate and sufficient.
- Recall and precision in the same period as the rule. E.g.: May to October 2026 add up to 370 positives; the rule flagged 1,250 accounts and got 140 right: recall 37.8%, precision 11.2%.
- D+N availability is out. E.g.: survey.nps_last (D+45) is out; 4 of 5 variables remain (80%).
- A partial label gives a condition, and a pending condition goes to the data lead. E.g.: #2026-41: the label does not mark downgrade (covers part): FEASIBLE WITH CONDITION; grid 4 + 4 + 3 + 5 = 16; pending condition goes to the data lead.
- A request with no one who acts gets no score. E.g.: #2026-42: RETURNED, with no classification and no score; the decision is about candidates (individuals): BIAS AND LEGAL REVIEW.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Do this
  1. 1Download the 4 sample files and upload them to Input
  2. 2In Diana's panel, click ▶
  3. 3Open the file MODELFEASIBLE_….md in Output

# Rules in use by the areas

## Customer Success
Rule: an account with no login for 21 days goes onto the risk list.
Measurement from May to October 2026: the rule flagged 1,250 accounts; 140 of them canceled within 60 days.

## People
Rule: manual screening by resume, with no recorded measurement.

Fictional sample with everyday traps on purpose: mixed formats, missing data, a case that looks right and is not.

Step 5 of 5 · Use

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3For each new request, export the form as intake.json to the Input folder, with the dictionaries, the aggregated counts and the rules in use, and click ▶
  4. 4Replace the bands, the grid and the classification order in the knowledge base with your committee's
  5. 5After a few reviewed opinions, connect Slack to send the questions to the requester, with the data lead's approval
Done when
Columns your files need
intake.json
dictionaries.csv
counts.csv

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The assessment does not decide the queue: the committee decides and the agent delivers the evidence, because a request with few positives may still be worth it for its financial impact. The agent does not access production databases or receive customer samples; it works with dictionaries and aggregated counts. A request involving a decision about people, such as credit, hiring or individual pricing, comes out flagged for bias and legal review, even when it is technically feasible.

Common mistakes

  • Assessing feasibility by the number of rows instead of the number of positive events; 30 positives a month cannot sustain a classifier.
  • Accepting a label annotated by hand by whoever would use the model, without checking delay and criteria.
  • Skipping the question 'who acts and with what capacity per month'.
  • Not measuring the existing rule before the model; without a benchmark, any AUC looks like a win.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Projects abandoned after startingfrom 4 in 9 to 0 to 1 in 10 per yearestimate based on the described routine
Scientist hours on abandoned projectsfrom 800 to 1,600 per year to fewer than 200estimate based on the described routine
Agreement of the assessment with the actual outcome of the 9 projects4 out of 4 abandoned classified as not feasible and 4 out of 5 delivered as feasibleestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Assessment of request #2026-31, Customer Success area. REQUEST: predict which accounts will cancel in the next 60 days so the success team can act.
DECISION SUPPORTED: choose 40 accounts per month for proactive contact. WHO ACTS: 6 account managers. OK.
LABEL: cancellation recorded in billing; reliable, but 'downgrade' is not treated as cancellation and accounts for 35% of revenue loss according to the dictionary. WARNING: decide whether downgrade goes into the target.
POSITIVE VOLUME: 62 cancellations per month across 4,100 active accounts; 'below 100' band: the model tends to be unstable; 18 months of history give 1,100 positives, enough for a first model with temporal validation.
DATA AT DECISION TIME: product usage, tickets and billing available at D-1; NPS arrives 45 days late and cannot be used as a variable.
EXISTING BASELINE: the team's current rule 'no login in 21 days'; precision never measured. Estimate of the rule on the history provided: captures 41% of cancellations with 12% precision.
CLASSIFICATION: FEASIBLE WITH CONDITION. Conditions: decide the target (cancellation, or cancellation and downgrade) and measure the current rule for 4 weeks as the benchmark to beat. GRID SCORE: 14 out of 20 (value 5, data 4, label 3, action 2).
QUESTIONS FOR THE REQUESTER: 2 (target; real contact capacity per month).
